sync.prompt: Choose which Notion databases to sync

dimensions.label: Databases
dimensions.note: No new node: notion-search_pages-1 already lists what a person picks from, browse_input pins it to data sources, and option_mapping turns each result into a scope option.

page.label: Pages
page.note: A row in a data source is a page, and its text lives in its blocks, so the body costs a second call per page - Notion has no endpoint that lists rows with their content. The watermark rides inside Notion's own timestamp filter: the static list_input carries the whole filter with an epoch floor, and the cursor overwrites the on_or_after inside it, because a Notion filter is invalid without its sibling `timestamp` key. Sorted ascending, so a walk resumes forward. NOT LIVE-TESTED: the dev integration currently has no page shared with it, so this recipe is written from Notion's documented shapes and the node schemas, not from a recorded run. Trash is not detected: a trashed page simply stops coming back from a query, and query_databases-1 returns no in_trash field, so nothing here can mark it deleted. That needs either the field on the node or a full re-list strategy.

notes.sync: The unit is a DATA SOURCE, not a database. Since API version 2025-09-03 a Notion database is a container of one or more data sources, the search object filter takes "data_source" and no longer accepts "database", and a query addresses the data source. So the honest thing to store in sync_scope is the data source id, which is also what notion-query_databases-1 reads. The picker still says "Databases", because that is the word a person sees in Notion's own UI.
notes.auth: Notion has no granular OAuth scopes and takes no scope parameter, so `scopes` is empty on purpose and no node declares required_scopes. What an integration may do is set on the integration itself in the developer portal (read content, update content, insert content, read comments, insert comments, and a user-information level); what it may reach is whatever a person picks on the consent screen. Calling outside the configured capabilities answers 403, and a page nobody shared answers 404. The token exchange uses HTTP Basic with client_id:client_secret and returns a non-expiring access_token with no refresh_token.
notes.api_version: Every request carries `Notion-Version: 2026-03-11`, sent from notion_requests.ts. Notion versions its REST API by a dated header, not by a path segment, and refuses a request without one. Staying on an older version is not the safe choice: Notion documents that queries, page creation and relation writes start failing on any database a person later gives a second data source.
notes.version_history: 2022-06-28 -> 2025-09-03 (a database became a container of one or more data sources; queries and page parents address the data source, and the search object filter takes "data_source" instead of "database") -> 2026-03-11 (`archived` renamed to `in_trash`; the flat `after` parameter on block append became a `position` object).
notes.rate_limits: Notion documents an average of three requests per second per connection, with short bursts above it tolerated, plus a workspace-wide ceiling that scales with the workspace plan. Over the limit answers 429 with Retry-After in seconds, which the runtime's rate limiter honours. 180 rpm with a burst of 3 is that average written down.
notes.no_batch_endpoints: Notion has no batch endpoints. One request creates one page, queries one data source, reads one block's children. Every plural node here runs its contract on the runtime's fan_out, so a batch of N costs N round trips and the node descriptions say so.
notes.payload_limits: 2000 characters per rich text span, 100 elements per block array, 1000 blocks and 500 KB per payload, page_size at most 100, and paginated property arrays truncated to 25 items inside a page object.
notes.mcp_verdict: Notion's hosted MCP server (mcp.notion.com) was checked against the batch law and fails it. Of about 37 tools only notion-create-pages and notion-move-pages take arrays; notion-fetch, notion-update-page, comments, views and every database mutation are one-object-in. It also answers in Notion-flavored Markdown rather than stable JSON, and caps at 180 requests per minute per user with keyword search at 30. So these nodes are native REST against api.notion.com/v1.
